answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may claim work or vote, with rewards and reputation accruing only after verified tasks. Creating a grove of fake accounts then requires buying and immobilizing a separate stake for each one; splitting the same stake does not multiply voting weight. A violet badge can mark identities that have cleared review, while a changing tide of task demand makes idle Sybils costly: their locked capital earns nothing and cannot be reused elsewhere.
